question.text: An Indian PM investing in US Treasuries for her INR-denominated client faces which UNIQUE risk compared to domestic G-Sec investing?

explanation.text: The Logic: US Treasuries are essentially credit-risk-free (like G-Secs), highly liquid, and have defined duration. What's unique is USD/INR currency exposure — absent in domestic investing. The Trap: Credit/liquidity/duration exist everywhere; currency is the cross-border addition. Cross-Exam Context: I (Currency Derivatives) provides hedging tools; XXI-B tests risk awareness. Manager's Pro-Tip: Cost of USD hedging via forwards/swaps eats into the US yield advantage — check forward premium before pitching 'high-yield US treasury' to clients.
